handback.t:
W18 result: the hnsw_rs 0.3.4 reverse-edge bug is real. It makes about 0.7-2.4% of stored items permanently unfindable, not the ~6% the R2 proposal guessed. The one-line patch fixes it completely, and I measured a no-crate-change workaround.

**The defect.** `reverse_update_neighborhood_simple` (hnsw.rs line 1245) writes reverse edges at `l_n = new_point.p_id.0` (the new point's top level) instead of the loop layer `l`. I changed that one line in a vendored copy of the crate to `l as usize`.

**Measured over 200 builds per variant (120 iid, 80 clustered), M=16, ef_construction=200, cosine, sequential `insert_slice` as neural-mesh does:**
- **Unpatched:** every build loses items, measured as items that are not their own top-1 at ef=512, k=1.
  - iid: 1k d32 0.70%, 1k d384 0.665%, 5k d32 0.667%, 5k d384 0.92%, 30k d32 1.14%, 30k d384 2.41% (a hard geometry).
  - Clustered data: 1.14-1.33%.
  - All 25,932 misses are level>=1 points (about 6.2% of items); there were zero misses on level-0 points.
  - The lost items are also absent from the top-10 at ef=512, so raising ef cannot recover them. Roughly 11-30% of level>=1 points end up with layer-0 in-degree 0.
- **Patched:** 0 misses, 0 in-degree-0 points and 0 unreachable points in all 200 builds.
- **Recall@10 vs brute force, patched minus unpatched, 95% CI over 20 seeds:**
  - 1k d32: +.0151 (ef 50) / +.0123 (ef 100) / +.0103 (ef 200).
  - 5k d384: +.0102 / +.0171 / +.0240.
  - 30k d32: +.0238 / +.0247 / +.0233, with ef=200 going from .9758 to .9991.
  - 30k d384: +.0018 / +.0058 / +.0086, but absolute recall is only about .52 in that regime.
  - Clustered data: +.009 to +.014, with patched recall at 1.000 for 1k and 5k.
  - The unpatched recall ceiling of about .985-.99 explains part of the H2 ".96-.99" figure.

**Exposure in neural-mesh.** Defaults are flat, so it is exposed only when an HNSW backend is chosen. The opt-in paths are `HnswIndex` in `src/memory.rs`, `HnswRm` (`LongKind::Hnsw`) in `src/tiered.rs`, `CaseRouter::with_index(HnswIndex)` in `src/casebased.rs`, `IndexKind::Hnsw` in `src/workmem.rs`, and the bins `memory_lab`, `memory_bench` and `r3_store`. `knowledge.rs` has no HNSW.

Through neural-mesh's own wrappers (unpatched crate, 5k d384, 20 builds):
- `HnswIndex::add`: 1.10% of items not their own top-1 at the default ef=64.
- `add_batch` (parallel): 1.08%.
- `HnswRm::add`: 1.04%.
- `HnswRm` after removing 10% of items and `compact()`: 0.94%, so compaction re-triggers the bug.
- If HNSW is used, about 1% of stored lessons or cases are silently unretrievable by similarity search.

**Workaround without a crate change.** Call `hnsw.modify_level_scale(0.2)` right after `Hnsw::new` and before the first insert. It needs `let mut` and prints two lines to stdout per call.
- 0 misses in 78 builds across the six cells (3-20 builds each).
- Recall and latency match the patched crate up to 30k: 5k d32 recall .9850/.9993/1.0000, and 850 vs 892 us per query at 30k d32.
- Factor 0.5 is not enough (0.012-0.022% still lost).
- The alternative is vendoring the one-line patch via `[patch.crates-io]`, which is also what ruvector-core does.
- Not recommended: jittered double-insert and jittered re-insert leave 0.02-0.10% lost and hurt recall at low ef. Exact-duplicate re-insert does not help; I only smoke-tested it on 3 seeds at 1k d32 and did not save it to CSV.
- Larger ef and insertion order have no effect.

**Limits.**
- Data are synthetic (iid Gaussian and cluster mixtures), no real embeddings.
- Wrapper-vs-patched was not run, because it needs a Cargo `[patch]` and I did not edit `Cargo.toml`. The patched-crate harness uses the identical call sequence and distance.
- The workaround was only measured up to N=30k; the 30k d384 cell had 3 builds and 30k d32 had 5.
- Levels use an OS-seeded RNG, so reruns are not byte-identical. The invariants to check are patched = 0 and unpatched > 0 in every build.

I did not touch `Cargo.toml`, `src/*.rs` or the cargo registry, and made no commits or downloads. The vendored copy was read first: no build.rs, no network or telemetry code.
